title: Decisiveness amid Uncertainty
coreMove: make a grounded call before perfect clarity arrives, then keep the team ready to revise as facts change
sourcePressure: Leaders must make timely decisions with incomplete information, avoiding both hesitation and reckless speed.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: decisive leaders are certain and fast
sourceAnchorsNote: source contains no named anecdote for this chapter

counterintuition: leadership is harder than it looks
tryThisNow: ask yourself how to be a better leader

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: prevents the timestamp+named-protagonist template from dominating the chapter

exampleSpecs.domain: river regatta with lightning risk and boats already staged
exampleSpecs.audience: a race director balancing safety, fairness, and impatient crews
exampleSpecs.stakes: waiting too long exposes crews, while canceling too early wastes the only race window
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director uses the last reliable radar scan, the lightning distance rule, and rescue-boat readiness to call a thirty-minute hold, then names the update point
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a lightning-distance card flutters beside numbered bow tags on the dock

exampleSpecs.domain: vineyard frost fan activation before the forecast settles
exampleSpecs.audience: a vineyard manager deciding whether to spend fuel before dawn
exampleSpecs.stakes: waiting for perfect forecast can lose the lower block crop
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager compares leaf temperature, low-block history, and fuel limit, starts fans in the vulnerable rows, and checks again after twenty minutes
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You are close enough to see this: leaf thermometer reads just above freezing under a headlamp.

exampleSpecs.domain: airport gate operation when a crew member is missing
exampleSpecs.audience: a gate manager with passengers boarding and dispatch giving partial updates
exampleSpecs.stakes: boarding too soon or too late can both create cascading delays
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager decides to hold boarding for twelve minutes, tells passengers the concrete next update, and prepares the aircraft swap if crew timing misses the window
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The first thing you register is physical: crew-status tile stays gray above a line of passengers at gate C17.

exampleSpecs.domain: pediatric emergency department considering transfer before final lab results
exampleSpecs.audience: an ER attending with a sick child and incomplete diagnostics
exampleSpecs.stakes: delay can close the transfer window, but premature transfer has risks
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the attending states what is known, what would change the decision, starts the transfer call now, and leaves room to cancel if the lab returns differently
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Hold there," someone says. Ambulance bay light reflects across a half-completed lab panel.

exampleSpecs.domain: elementary school dismissal during wildfire smoke
exampleSpecs.audience: a principal deciding between outdoor pickup and indoor release
exampleSpecs.stakes: families need direction before air-quality data fully stabilizes
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the principal uses the current air-quality monitor, bus timing, and nurse guidance to switch to indoor pickup, then revises the plan when wind changes
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Later, the team will trace the lesson back to this: air-quality monitor blinks orange beside a stack of dismissal placards.

exampleSpecs.domain: mining conveyor line after a vibration spike
exampleSpecs.audience: a site supervisor balancing production pressure and mechanical uncertainty
exampleSpecs.stakes: a bearing failure can injure workers if the line keeps running for proof
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the supervisor halts the conveyor on the spike plus noise report, assigns inspection, and sets the restart condition before production leaders press for speed
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What changes once this is in front of everyone: vibration readout jumps red while ore dust settles on the stop cord?

skillTargets: make a timely call from enough evidence without pretending certainty
spot hesitation and reckless speed as opposite failures
choose revision triggers after action begins

tryThisNowSpec: For a pending call, write what you know, what would change the call, the latest useful decision time, and the first revision trigger.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following 'concrete anchor -> abstract rule -> elaboration'
